scope.selected_call_shape: one explicit positional URL argument with no required keyword arguments
scope.note: This v0 models only the selected public requests.get(url) call form used by the controlled benchmark. Requests 0.2.0 is the first confirmed public release boundary for this selected form: the package root re-exports requests.core and requests.core defines get(url, ...). The same selected form remains present in Requests 2.32.3 and the fixed 2.32.4 release. This API scope does not redefine the vulnerability range <2.32.4.

version_rules.evidence_ref: Requests 0.2.0 / 2.32.3 / 2.32.4 official release and source evidence
version_rules.evidence_note: Requests 0.2.0 is the first confirmed public release boundary for the selected requests.get(url) form. Its package root re-exports requests.core, where get(url, ...) is defined. The same one-positional-URL form remains supported immediately before and after the vulnerability fix boundary.

scope_start.observation: requests.__init__ re-exports requests.core, and requests.core defines get(url, params={}, headers={}, auth=None), making requests.get available at the package root.

vulnerable_boundary.observation: requests.get remains defined as get(url, params=None, **kwargs) immediately before the fixed release.

fixed_boundary.observation: requests.get remains defined as get(url, params=None, **kwargs) in the fixed release; the security fix changes netrc host lookup semantics rather than removing this public API.

sources.claim: The Requests release history labels 0.2.0 as Birth and 0.0.1 as Frustration / Conception.
Requests 0.2.0 package root imports all public symbols from requests.core.
Requests 0.2.0 defines get(url, params={}, headers={}, auth=None) in requests.core.
Requests 2.32.4 continues to define get(url, params=None, **kwargs), showing that the vulnerability fix does not remove the selected public API.
